gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-multani: A splayed c terminal and tube-like strokes with no swelling anywhere give Tilt Neon its glow. Noto Sans Multani counters with a lofty x-height and an e that gapes wide at its terminal.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: Tilt Neon draws every letter as a tube of constant width, with no pen-angle modulation at all. Noto Sans Myanmar settles into a thick, heavy-looking strip of text, its broad c openings keeping long lines welcoming.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Commanding is how Tilt Neon lands, its marker-nib line ignoring direction and its x-height running large. And Noto Sans Nabataean follows with lowercase standing almost cap-tall and wide s curves, so the two feel sized for each other.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-nag-mundar: Tilt Neon squeezes its letters out like toothpaste in one steady line, with a splayed c terminal. Noto Sans Nag Mundari follows with half-unwrapped c and s shapes and lowercase that nearly rivals the capitals.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-nandinagar: Approachable, first of all, in the body. Tilt Neon cuts flat, stencil-like shapes from a single weight, while Noto Sans Nandinagari keeps its openings generous and its big lowercase friendly beneath it.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-newa: Tilt Neon's n arches are as thick as the stems beside them, a flat tube-like construction with short ascenders and a large x-height. Noto Sans Newa runs on easily, its open e and tall bowls keeping a long page light.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Noto Sans Nushu holds its terminals far from the stroke body and towers with a huge x-height. Tilt Neon, meanwhile, is best as a plain stripe of constant ink, bold and commanding, while Noto Sans Nushu is best at modern, spacious text.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Bold is the word for Tilt Neon, whose letters look made of rods rather than carved blades. And Noto Sans Ogham reads cleanly over a long passage, its wide-gapped e and tall bodies making the lowercase feel sturdy.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Tilt Neon cuts every letter at a single depth, like an engraver who never goes deeper in places. And Noto Sans Ol Chiki holds its curve tails well back, so a long passage settles into solid, clean blocks of sans-serif.
